openings.claim: Pencil assigned patterns and exact quantity checklists on envelopes; mark quantities after filling, retaining trays and samples. This may reduce quantity omissions and expose assignments.
openings.discriminator: Matched mixtures distinguish quantity confusion from shared-tray interference. Local loose materials eliminating omissions while correctly used shared-tray checklists retain them defeats the central explanation.
openings.probe: Compare equal matched batches: incumbent, shared trays with checks, and local loose materials without checks. Alternate order; verify contents and tally omissions, crossing reaches, and preparation/filling/checking time within constraints.
openings.uncertainty: Exact quantities must be available from samples; arrangements must fit. O4's mixture is unknown. Writing costs, later depletion, and transfer to 60 kits remain untested.

openings.claim: Pencil explicit material names and specified dimensions onto existing tray tags, if writable, to test whether ambiguous identification causes shared-material omissions.
openings.discriminator: Fewer identification errors and omissions support identification ambiguity; correct identification with unchanged filling omissions defeats it. Quantity loss remains a rival.
openings.probe: Assemble twelve kits per original/clarified-tag condition with matched mixtures and exchanged order, counting them toward 60. Tally identification errors, omissions, exact contents and all preparation/checking time; record final distribution corrections.
openings.uncertainty: Tag writability, matched allocation and packet/checking footprint are unconfirmed. Clarification need not reduce crossings, reveal unopened stock, or expose envelope assignments.

lineage.reason: Preserves quantity guidance, assignment labeling, integrated checking and interference rival.
Preserves distinct identity clarification and quantity/filling rival.

decision: Both are unproven probes from an entirely synthetic fixture. Preserve specified quantities/dimensions; use exactly two volunteers, at most 90 minutes, the existing 180-by-75-centimetre table, envelopes and supplies, with no purchases/equipment. Picking versus filling remains unresolved. Small-batch success cannot establish all 60 correctly assigned complete kits before the workshop with at most one distribution correction.
